versions.skill: main @ 2026-10-29 (3,629 B; sha256 in fixtures/skills/SHA256SUMS); companion files tests.md / mocking.md not fetched, stated in the arm-B prompt
versions.agent: Claude Code subagents, same session model in both arms

install.command: claude plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official (or copy SKILL.md)

fixtures: fixtures/14-tdd: task/README.md (spec of src/pricing.mjs: toGrams, pricePerKg, formatMoney, kcalPer100g, daysSupply, compare with rounding/currency/locale/leap-year rules, 7 visible examples, one smoke test), hidden/cases.mjs (25 named case groups), grade.mjs (runs under TZ=Pacific/Auckland on purpose), reference/ (25/25), calibration/ (two fresh one-shot plain runs by the builder: 21/25 on the final README after re-grading, 24/25), KEY.md
design: Arm A = plain subagent implements from the spec; Arm B = same prompt + SKILL.md inline (no interactive user: seams written to SEAMS.md and proceed). 3 reps per arm, fresh copies, concurrent. Score = hidden case groups passed / 25. Hardening: the builder removed giveaway hints and added three rules after a 25/25 one-shot; a second fresh one-shot still scored 24/25, so the 40-80 % target was not reached without making the spec vague (noise for both arms) or adding tricks, which the brief forbids. Reported as a ceiling-limited trial.

baseline.failed_case_in_every_run: D03 (daysSupply with an untrimmed ISO date ' 2028-02-28 '; the common 'trim input' rule applies, every run rejected it)

candidate_default.config: Arm B with the tdd skill
candidate_default.observed: Arm B visibly followed the skill: SEAMS.md written in 3/3, one test file per seam, red-before-green cycles, 15-23 tests vs 7 in arm A, two runs corrected their own wrong test literals against the spec instead of bending the code.

limits: Ceiling: both arms at 24/25 in every rep; the one missed case is identical across all six runs, so the hidden set measures one spec reading, not skill effect.
n = 3 per arm; wall time has shared-CPU noise (up to 12 concurrent agents).
Token counts include each subagent's fixed context; only the A-B difference is meaningful.
The skill's 'confirm seams with the user' step had no user; the adaptation (write SEAMS.md and proceed) removes the one step that could change the outcome in an interactive session.
verdict: REJECT for spec-to-module tasks of this size (no gain, +11 % tokens, +180 % tool calls, +20 % time); the extra tests it leaves behind are the only tangible output
reason: Same hidden score (0.96) in all six runs. The skill triples the number of tool calls and leaves ~3x more tests, at +11 % tokens and +20 % wall time. Whether those tests pay off on later changes is not measured here.
do_not_adopt_notes: As a default for well-specified modules: no measured quality gain. Worth a second look only where the team values the test suite itself (regression coverage), which this trial did not score.
